newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Catch-up in banks and tech stocks.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Catch-up in banks and tech stocks.

text.p: The banking and technology sectors, which had been left behind in the market's strong bounce this week, were playing catch-up today, spurring interest in call options, traders said.

"Compaq (Computer Corp ) is coming back, so is Intel (Corp ) -- maybe there is something to this rally," said Michael Schwartz, a managing director of Oppenheimer & Co. "I guess it gives some credence to it."
Although the broader market pulled back into negative territory by late trade, banks and high-techs were resilient.
In many issues including index options, April calls, which expire on Friday, saw fresh buying and little rollover, traders said.

Compaq April 75.0 calls were among the most actively traded calls on the Pacific Stock Exchange (PSE), with turnover of 2,731 contracts by late afternoon. At one point, premium more than doubled to 1-3/4 from 5/8 as the stock touched a high of 76-3/8, up 3 on the day.
The contract expires in only one day, but for bullish traders its high gamma provided quick acceleration against a rally in the stock.

Similarly, Intel's April 135 call was among the busiest contracts on the American Stock Exchange (AMEX) on volume of 8,954 contracts. Premium tripled to a high of 4 from 1-3/16 as the stock peaked at 138-15/16, up 4-15/16.
Both Compaq and Intel stocks tumbled earlier in the week despite moderately positive earnings and a broad market rally.

Brian Belski, a vice president at Dain Bosworth, said the sector still looked shaky, even though investors still seemed to be looking at "ideas on the upside that would work." He noted that the selloff earlier in the week reflected a profound change in investor attitude toward some popular stocks.
"Investors are reacting now rather than...buying the stocks for later," he said.

Bank stocks were also up sharply today after steadily declining since early March on concerns over a tighter Federal Reserve monetary policy. The Philadelphia Stock Exchange's banking index .BKX was up 6.24 at 559.11 in late trade after rising as high as 566.25.
Option volume in BKX was modest but premiums on calls were plump. Premium on April 560 calls was quoted at around 2 in late trade after rising as high as 6-10/16 on turnover of 779 contracts.
"That's pretty high for an at-the-money contract expiring tomorrow," Schwartz at Oppenheimer said.
Citicorp and Chase Manhattan Corp saw some good interest in April and May calls. Belski said these stocks were bouncing off support levels but warned that it was too early to call a bottom yet.

Elsewhere, ADC Telecommunications Inc traded about 4,700 lots each in May 27.5 calls and 22.5 puts, topping PSE's most-ctives list. A trader in the ADC options crowd said an investor sold the puts and bought calls against the stock, which ended down 3/8 at 23-5/8, in a "risk reversal".
